references.title: WHO — The WHO AWaRe (Access, Watch, Reserve) antibiotic book (2022)

title: Antimicrobial Stewardship Assistant
short: Reviews antibiotic orders against local guidelines and culture results, and prompts timely de-escalation, IV-to-oral switch and duration review.
symptom: Antibiotics run longer and broader than needed
ingredient: A stewardship review list for the hospital pharmacist
directions: Connect antibiotic orders and microbiology results. Each morning the stewardship pharmacist gets a prioritized review list with suggested actions.
problem: Stewardship teams cannot review every antibiotic order daily; opportunities to narrow therapy, switch to oral or stop on time are missed.
why: Unnecessary broad-spectrum use drives antimicrobial resistance, adverse effects and cost.
solution: Matches each order with indication, culture and sensitivity results, renal function and local guidelines, then ranks patients where de-escalation, IV-to-oral switch, dose adjustment or stopping should be considered.
data: Local antibiotic guidelines and resistance patterns
limitations: Local guidelines and resistance data must stay current
review: The stewardship pharmacist and prescriber decide every change to therapy.
